paragraphs: A new study looked at children who miss school. It found a problem in poorer areas. In these schools, more absences have no reason given.
The study is from the ESRI, a research group in Ireland. It looked at schools in recent years.
In primary schools, about one in four absences had no reason. In schools in poorer city areas, it was 41%. In other schools, it was 23%.
In secondary schools, half of all absences had no reason. In schools in poorer areas, it was 60%.
A researcher said this is not fair for children. Without a reason, it is harder for schools to help. Children are still missing more school than before Covid.
sentZh: 一項新研究調查了缺課的孩子。
研究在較貧窮的地區發現了一個問題。
在這些學校，有更多缺席沒有說明理由。
這項研究來自愛爾蘭的研究機構ESRI。
它調查了近幾年的學校情況。
在小學，大約每四次缺席就有一次沒有理由。
在城市較貧窮地區的學校，比例是41%。
在其他學校，比例是23%。
在中學，所有缺席中有一半沒有理由。
在較貧窮地區的學校，比例是60%。
一位研究人員說，這對孩子不公平。
沒有理由，學校就更難提供幫助。
孩子們缺課的情況仍比新冠疫情前多。

paragraphs: Schools in poorer areas have more pupil absences with no reason given, a new study has found. The study was done by the ESRI, an Irish research institute.
The report looked at pupils who miss a lot of school. It used information collected by Tusla, the child and family agency.

In primary schools, about a quarter of absences had no explanation. In DEIS schools in cities, which get extra support because they serve poorer communities, the figure was 41%. In other schools, it was 23%. In secondary schools, half of all absences were unexplained. This rose to 60% in DEIS schools.
Researcher Anna Moya said this was a worry for equality. When schools do not know why a child is absent, it is harder to give the right help.
The number of primary pupils who missed more than 20 days fell from 22.1% to 19%. But more secondary students missed a lot of school. Overall, absences are still higher than before the pandemic.
sentZh: 一項新研究發現，較貧窮地區的學校有更多未說明理由的學生缺席。
這項研究由愛爾蘭研究機構ESRI進行。
報告調查了經常缺課的學生。
它使用了兒童與家庭事務局Tusla收集的資料。
在小學，大約四分之一的缺席沒有說明。
在城市中的DEIS學校（因服務較貧窮社區而獲得額外支援），這個數字是41%。
在其他學校則是23%。
在中學，所有缺席中有一半未說明原因。
在DEIS學校，這個比例升至60%。
研究員安娜·莫亞說，這在平等方面令人擔憂。
當學校不知道孩子為何缺席時，就更難給予適當的幫助。
缺課超過20天的小學生比例從22.1%降至19%。
但有更多中學生經常缺課。
整體而言，缺席情況仍高於疫情前。

paragraphs: Schools serving disadvantaged communities record a higher share of unexplained pupil absences, according to new research from the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI).
The study examined chronic absence, which means missing more than 20 school days in a year. It was based on data collected by Tusla's education support service.

At primary level, about a quarter of all absences were unexplained. In urban DEIS schools, which receive extra resources to tackle educational disadvantage, the proportion reached 41%, compared with 23% in other schools. At post-primary level, half of all absences had no explanation, rising to 60% in DEIS schools.
Researcher Anna Moya said the gap was a concern from an equality perspective, because it makes it more difficult to design support that meets each pupil's needs.

Chronic absence at primary level fell from 22.1% to 19% in the latest school year, but more than 8,000 additional post-primary students were chronically absent. Overall absence levels remain above those seen before the pandemic. The study found no meaningful difference between boys and girls.
sentZh: 根據經濟與社會研究所（ESRI）的新研究，服務弱勢社區的學校記錄到較高比例的無故學生缺席。
這項研究調查了長期缺席，也就是一年內缺課超過20天。
研究依據的是Tusla教育支援服務所收集的數據。
在小學階段，大約四分之一的缺席未說明原因。
在獲得額外資源以處理教育弱勢問題的城市DEIS學校，這個比例達到41%，其他學校則為23%。
在中學階段，一半的缺席沒有說明原因，在DEIS學校更升至60%。
研究員安娜·莫亞說，從平等的角度來看這個差距令人擔憂，因為它讓設計符合每位學生需求的支援變得更困難。
在最近一個學年，小學的長期缺席率從22.1%降至19%，但長期缺席的中學生增加了8,000多人。
整體缺席水準仍高於疫情前。
研究發現男生和女生之間沒有明顯差異。

paragraphs: Schools catering for disadvantaged communities grapple with a markedly higher proportion of unexplained pupil absences, new research from the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) has revealed.
The study scrutinised chronic absence, defined as missing more than 20 school days a year, drawing on data compiled by Tusla's education support service.

Roughly a quarter of absences at primary level went unexplained, but in urban DEIS schools, which are allocated additional resources to counter educational disadvantage, the figure soared to 41%, against 23% elsewhere. At post-primary level, fully half of absences lacked an explanation, climbing to 60% in DEIS schools.
Researcher Anna Moya warned that the disparity was troubling from an equality standpoint, since it hampers efforts to tailor interventions to individual pupils.

While chronic absence among primary pupils dipped from 22.1% to 19% in the latest school year, the ranks of chronically absent post-primary students swelled by more than 8,000. Absence levels have yet to revert to pre-pandemic norms. Notably, the researchers detected no meaningful gender divide.
